name: AEMET: meteorological warnings

frame.part: top of the page, no scrolling

capture_note: Requested from incident.archivist@: same address, 1280 x 1600 viewport, top of page. Until then the study page draws the callouts on an empty frame. No image is kept in git.
licence_for_showing_the_screenshot: AEMET allows reuse citing AEMET as the source without distorting the information (its legal notice): a screenshot with the credit fits.
summary: The fullest warnings page we saw: the next three days' level in the header of every page, a special notice in words, a map with a hazard filter and a time bar, and under it a matrix of regions against time. On the night of Charles it showed red for Extremadura and Castilla y León.

callouts.title: Three days, three dots, in the header
callouts.does_well: Wed 11 red, Thu 12 orange, Fri 13 yellow: the highest level of each of the next three days sits beside the menu on every page of the site.

callouts.title: The special notice, in words
callouts.does_well: One line above the map: "Aviso especial. Lluvias fuertes y persistentes, rachas muy fuertes y temporal marítimo." The forecasters' own headline before any colour.

callouts.title: Hazards as a filter
callouts.does_well: All, Wind, Rainfalls, Storms, Coastal: one click redraws the map for one hazard.

callouts.title: The map by warning zone
callouts.does_well: Zones smaller than provinces, in the four European colours; the red zone is visible at once among the orange.
callouts.fed_by: our own redraw from IPMA's JSON; district shapes from an open source

callouts.title: A time bar with play
callouts.does_well: Three day tabs (each "00-24h") and a play button that runs the map through time.

callouts.title: The matrix: regions against time
callouts.does_well: One row per region; the hazards in force as small icons framed in their level's colour; then one coloured cell per period across the three days. The whole country's next three days in one table. A feed icon on every row.
callouts.fed_by: incidents/2026-11-10-storm-charles/data/weather/warnings.json; for us the rows are Lisbon's hazards and then the decisions (incidents/2026-11-10-storm-charles/data/decisions/graph.json)

limits: The cookie banner was not dismissed and takes the top 120 px of the frame.
